question: What Speed Limit (R2-1) sign sizes are shown in Table 2B-1 for conventional single-lane, conventional multi-lane, expressway, and freeway applications?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Table 2B-1 (Regulatory Sign and Plaque Sizes, Sheet 1 of 6) lists the Speed Limit (R2-1) sign at 24 x 30 inches for single-lane conventional roads, 30 x 36 inches for multi-lane conventional roads, 36 x 48 inches for expressways, and 48 x 60 inches for freeways. The table also shows a minimum size of 18 x 24 inches and an oversized size of 30 x 36 inches for the R2-1 sign. Standards (mandatory): - While the text evidence does not quote the size values themselves as a Standard provision, the R2-1 sign's legend content is governed by Standard: "The Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (see Figure 2B-3) shall display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study. The speed limits displayed shall be in multiples of 5 mph." Visual evidence: - [Image 5] shows Table 2B-1 (Sheet 1 of 6), whose "Speed Limit / R2-1 / 2B.21" row reads: Conventional Road Single Lane 24 x 30; Multi-Lane 30 x 36; Expressway 36 x 48; Freeway 48 x 60; Minimum 18 x 24; Oversized 30 x 36. - [Image 1] (Figure 2B-3) illustrates the Speed Limit (R2-1) sign design and related speed limit plaques referenced by the table. Citations: - Page 109 - Figure 2B-3 (p.86) - Section 2B.21 Standard §13 (p.85)
gold_answer: 24 x 30, 30 x 36, 36 x 48, and 48 x 60 inches, respectively.
